name: manual_0f6905
claim: When testing an infinite-streaming (SSE) FastAPI/Starlette route, check for @app.middleware('http') decorators before assuming the test's own code is buggy -- that decorator registers Starlette's BaseHTTPMiddleware under the hood, which re-streams every response through an internal call_next() anyio memory-stream bridge that has a well-documented hang with infinite streaming bodies. No client-side httpx/TestClient timeout can interrupt it since the hang is server-side inside the middleware

decisions.notes: Spent significant time debugging what looked like a G7-specific SSE test hang (tried: async generator laziness fixes, httpx timeouts, ASGITransport direct calls) before tracing the actual root cause via a full Python traceback: orama-system's _control_plane_auth_middleware is registered via @app.middleware('http'), and Starlette's BaseHTTPMiddleware.call_next() bridge is what hangs, not the route code. Confirmed systemic (not G7-specific) by reproducing the identical hang on a completely unrelated pre-existing route (/events/peer-stream). Workaround: bypass TestClient/httpx streaming entirely for tests that only need to verify status/headers -- drive the raw ASGI protocol directly and capture just the http.response.start message, then cancel the task without waiting for the infinite body.
